boundary_rationale: A fresh discourse-imperative onset opens this row: oshb:Jer.51.6 (byte tier) נֻ֣סוּ מִתּ֣וֹךְ בָּבֶ֗ל וּמַלְּטוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ נַפְשׁ֔וֹ, “Flee out of the middle of Babylon! Everyone save his own life!” (web:Jer.51.6), shifting from the archers’ commission to a direct address urging escape. The golden-cup metaphor gives way to the quoted voice’s own words, “We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed” (web:Jer.51.9): oshb:Jer.51.9 and oshb:Jer.51.10 (byte tier) carry one continuous first-person-plural voice across the two verses, spliced, with no speech frame marking any change of speaker between them; a second-mouth impression is weighed here on the Hebrew itself, not on punctuation alone: אִ֣ישׁ לְאַרְצ֑וֹ (oshb:Jer.51.9, byte tier; that verse carries one single-witness ketiv/qere note on its opening verb, outside this splice) sends the voice to his own separate land, while בְצִיּ֔וֹן (oshb:Jer.51.10, byte tier) turns the same voice to one named homeland under a covenant title, a tension standing on both sides of this juncture; the nested single quotation the English rendering opens at 51:10 and not at 51:9 is a tier-4 punctuation fact that drives and corroborates nothing, disclosed and set aside. This same imperative-opened unit runs through that voice before the Median mobilization command opens fresh material.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the embedded quoted voice into its own row is defensible given its own shift in address, but it carries neither a fresh koh-amar nor a word-event formula of its own, so folding it under the shared flight command reads more conservatively.
literature_type_guess: flight command and foreign lament oracle
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: oshb:Jer.51.9 (ketiv/qere) carries a ketiv/qere note on its opening verb (one, per the inventory), the position read from the verse bytes, where the doubled reading stands verse-initially: רפאנו רִפִּ֣ינוּ. The quoted voice is embedded speech within the ongoing narratorial oracle, not a fresh frame-owner in the koh-amar sense.

boundary_rationale: A second discourse-imperative onset opens this row on a verse-initial imperative: oshb:Jer.51.11 (byte tier) הָבֵ֣רוּ הַחִצִּים֮ מִלְא֣וּ הַשְּׁלָטִים֒, “Make the arrows sharp! Hold the shields firmly!” (web:Jer.51.11), mobilizing the kings of the Medes against Babylon. This verse-initial position is the discriminator this reading applies: the mid-verse imperative clusters at oshb:Jer.51.8 and oshb:Jer.51.12 stand after their own verse-opening words and do not open units under this reading, while the verse-initial imperative at 51:11 does. The unit carries through the direct address to Babylon herself (oshb:Jer.51.13, byte tier, one single-witness ketiv/qere note) to its close at oshb:Jer.51.14 (byte tier) נִשְׁבַּ֛ע יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּנַפְשׁ֑וֹ, “Yahweh of Armies has sworn by himself” (web:Jer.51.14), where a single-witness setumah marks the section end.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row back to include the flight command and lament material would track one decree running straight through from the destroying wind onward, but the fresh imperative mobilizing the besiegers marks its own discourse frame.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: oshb:Jer.51.13 carries its own single-witness ketiv/qere note (one, per the inventory), separate from the denser cluster at oshb:Jer.51.34 (five notes, single-witness inventory); the row closes on YHWH’s own self-sworn oath rather than a further koh-amar or word-event onset, and the following unit’s own onset stands at oshb:Jer.51.15 (byte tier) עֹשֵׂ֥ה אֶ֨רֶץ֙ בְּכֹח֔וֹ, the participial doxology onset, so the close carries evidence beyond the single-witness setumah mark alone.

boundary_rationale: This span opens immediately after the book’s own colophon closes the preceding frame, עַד הֵ֖נָּה דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָֽהוּ (oshb:Jer.51.64, byte tier), “Thus far are the words of Jeremiah” (web:Jer.51.64) — the tier-1 signal standing at this seam, alongside the regnal age-at-accession formula that opens the appendix on Zedekiah’s own reign: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַחַ֤ת שָׁנָה֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וְאַחַ֤ת עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ חמיטל חֲמוּטַ֥ל בַּֽת יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מִלִּבְנָֽה (oshb:Jer.52.1, byte; a ketiv/qere pair sits over the mother’s name here, detailed below), matching “Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign. He reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.” (web:Jer.52.1). A regnal evaluation follows in its own verse, וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוֹיָקִֽים (oshb:Jer.52.2, byte) — “He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.” (web:Jer.52.2) — before the span closes on the rebellion report that sets the chapter’s crisis in motion, כִּ֣י עַל אַ֣ף יְהוָ֗ה הָֽיְתָה֙ בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה עַד הִשְׁלִיכ֥וֹ אוֹתָ֖ם מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑יו וַיִּמְרֹ֥ד צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּמֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל (oshb:Jer.52.3, byte), matching “For through Yahweh’s anger this happened in Jerusalem and Judah, until he had cast them out from his presence. Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.” (web:Jer.52.3). A paseq stands in this closing verse, oshb:Jer.52.3 (single-witness WLC; seg layer; a bare count, position not recorded). No fresh dating notice interrupts the chain from the accession formula to the rebellion report, so the three verses stay one span.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this opening span through the siege's dated onset that follows was rejected because the accession formula, the regnal evaluation, and the rebellion report form a closed backstory unit before any fresh dated action begins.
literature_type_guess: regnal accession notice with evaluation and rebellion report

device_notes: A setumah at oshb:Jer.51.64 closes the preceding frame; the mark carries single-witness WLC attestation, and the Prophets-addendum ruling holds it to tier-3 strength — weak corroboration, nothing more — so it drives nothing here, and its absence would prove nothing. The queen mother’s name carries a ketiv/qere pair at oshb:Jer.52.1 (single-witness WLC): the consonantal text reads חמיטל where the received reading is חֲמוּטַ֥ל, the two forms differing in the letter standing for the name’s internal vowel. Zedekiah’s name recurs in the long tsidqiyahu spelling six times across this chapter (sweep: 6 verses), and in this span it stands twice, at oshb:Jer.52.1 and oshb:Jer.52.3, rather than the short tsidqiyah form the book attests elsewhere. The regnal evaluation measures Zedekiah against a named predecessor rather than a general standard, a comparison this chapter’s own bytes do not repeat for him.
